scenario: AITA for leaving to see my GF when my sister told me not to when she was "in charge"? | My mom is gone for a class thing in another state, and my dad is on a business trip so its just me, my sister and my brother all alone in the house. My sister is 18, I am 17 and my brother is 12, I don't know why but my parents still felt the need to leave my sister "in charge" while they were both gone. My sister lets the power go to her head and while she can generally make my little brother obey her she has a tougher time with me. On Sunday I was gonna go out with my GF for dinner, and my sister stopped me saying that I can't leave. When asked its cause "she said so", I laughed at that and I thought she was joking but she just kept looking and I knew it was a joke. I told her she can boss (little brother's name) around but she can't boss me, and I went out with my GF. I guess my younger brother heard all the commotion and called mom saying we were "fighting" and when I came home and my mom called me she said that I'm grounded and have to dow what my sister says cause she's "in charge". I protested as best as I could but she wasn't having it and grounded me for disobeying my sister who is a pseudo parent while they are away. I just dropped it cause its not worth arguing any point with my mom. AITA here? EDIT:My brother told me afterwards that he was the one that told mom, I forgave him cause I mean I can't be mad at that little turd for too long

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing or not in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. My parents left me, my sister, and my brother alone at home. My sister is 18, I'm 17, and my brother is 12. My parents made my sister "in charge" while they were away. I guess that means she's supposed to take care of us and make sure everything is okay. On Sunday, I wanted to go out with my girlfriend for dinner. My sister told me I couldn't leave. When I asked why, she said, "Because I said so." At first, I thought she was joking, but she wasn't. I told her she can boss around my little brother but not me, and I went out with my girlfriend anyway. When I came home, my younger brother had told my mom about the "fight," and my mom called me, saying I'm grounded and have to do what my sister says because she's "in charge." I tried to protest, but my mom wasn't having it, and I got grounded for disobeying my sister who's acting like a pseudo-parent while they're away. I'm wondering if I did the right thing by going out with my girlfriend despite my sister's orders. Is it AITA (Ask if I'm the Asshole) here? Did I overreact? Should I have respected my sister's authority more? First, I need to consider the dynamics of the situation. My sister is 18, and I'm 17. She's technically older, but only by a year. My parents left her in charge, but does that mean she has the authority to make decisions about my activities? I mean, she's not a parent, and I'm almost an adult myself. When my sister told me I couldn't go out with my girlfriend, I felt like she was overstepping. I told her she can boss around my little brother but not me. That seems reasonable because my little brother is younger and might need more guidance, but I'm almost an adult and should have some autonomy. However, my mom grounded me for disobeying my sister. That makes me feel like my mom is supporting my sister's authority, even though I feel like I'm being treated like a child. Is it fair for my sister to have that kind of control over me? Should I have respected her authority more, even if I disagree with her decision? On the other hand, my sister might have felt the pressure of being "in charge" and took it too seriously. She might have been trying to assert her authority, but it backfired when I didn't comply. My mom's reaction to grounding me for not obeying my sister complicates things further. I also need to consider the impact on my relationship with my sister and my mom. By going out despite her orders, I might have caused unnecessary tension. But by standing up for my autonomy, I'm asserting my right to make my own decisions, especially since I'm almost an adult. Maybe I should have communicated better with my sister instead of dismissing her authority outright. If I had talked to her about why I wanted to go out and tried to find a compromise, things might have gone differently. But in the heat of the moment, it's easy to react impulsively. In the end, I got grounded, which was a consequence of my actions. I had to accept that and move on. It's not worth arguing further with my mom, as she's already made her decision. But I still wonder if I did the right thing by asserting my independence or if I should have respected my sister's authority more. I think the key here is balancing respect for the person in charge with asserting my own autonomy. Since I'm almost an adult, I should have some say in my activities, but I also need to respect the rules set by my parents when they're away. Maybe next time, I can find a middle ground by communicating my needs and understanding my sister's perspective. Overall, I don't think I was entirely wrong to want to go out with my girlfriend, but I could have handled the situation more maturely by discussing it with my sister instead of dismissing her authority outright. That way, I could have maintained respect for her role while asserting my own independence.
